title: Show it vs hand it back
idea: TOOL: print SHOWS a value on screen; return HANDS a value back to the caller. They are not the same.

exercises.prompt: Two different jobs: putting a value on the SCREEN, and giving a value BACK to the caller. Which does each?
options: print shows on screen; return hands back to the caller
exercises.explanation: print = show on screen. return = hand a value back so the caller can use it. Different jobs, different words.
Only return hands a value back to store. give(5) returns 5 into x; show(5) prints and leaves x as None.

exercises.prompt: print puts text on the screen but does not give a value back to the caller.
exercises.explanation: Right. print's job is display. If you want a value to reuse, that is return's job.

exercises.prompt:
def give(n):
    return n

x = give(5)

Does anything appear on screen?
exercises.explanation: return hands 5 back into x but shows nothing. You would need print(x) to see it on screen.

exercises.prompt:
def show(n):
    print(n)

show(5)

Does anything appear on screen?
exercises.explanation: show prints n, so 5 appears. print's job is exactly to put the value on the screen.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to its job.

pairs.right: hand a value back to the caller

exercises.explanation: print displays; return hands back. Keeping these straight avoids the most common function mix-up.

exercises.prompt: You want to store a sub-plan's answer and do more math with it. Which do you need?
exercises.explanation: Only a returned value can be stored and reused. A printed value is shown and then gone.

exercises.prompt: You just want to SEE the answer on screen and nothing more. Which is enough?
exercises.explanation: If you only need to display it, print does the job. return matters when the caller must reuse the value.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: you have used print since the very first unit. What is genuinely NEW about return?
options: It gives a value back instead of just showing it
exercises.explanation: print is old news - it shows. return is the new idea: handing a value back so your program can keep using it.

exercises.prompt: A sub-plan can both print AND return - but they do different things.
exercises.explanation: Yes. It could print a message for the user and also return a value for the caller. Two separate jobs.
